body:
## Problem

`unrolled_filter`, `unrolled_split`, and `unrolled_unique` are reductions that
push items into a tuple accumulator, so the accumulator's type changes at every
step. For long or complexly typed iterators, Julia inference's recursion-widening
heuristics widen the accumulator, and the resulting dynamic dispatch and heap
allocation cannot be compiled for GPUs. This broke ClimaAtmos AMIP runs through
ClimaCore's use of `unrolled_filter` in GPU kernels (`InvalidIRError` with
`gpu_gc_pool_alloc` and `jl_f__apply_iterate` in `unrolled_push_into`).

## Fix

Implement all three functions in terms of `unrolled_flatmap`, which maps each
item to an empty or singleton iterator based only on that item's type, so no
recursively growing type is inferred. `unrolled_unique` keeps an item when no
preceding item has the same value of `f` — quadratically many comparisons, but
the pushing reduction it replaces was also quadratic.

Semantics are unchanged. Version bumped to 0.1.10.

Also fixed one unrelated CI error related to PrettyTables v3
incompatibility in `test/test_and_analyze.jl`.
title: fix: implement filter, split, and unique in terms of unrolled_flatmap
